metaData.originalTitle: 让 Skill 自己训练自己：8 阶段 Loop、3 层评测、5 维 AND 门控，从此实现自进化
metaData.title: Let Skill Train Itself: 8-Stage Loop, 3-Tier Evaluation, 5-Dimensional AND Gating for Self-Evolution
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This paper proposes and implements a self-evolving framework called skill-evolver, which integrates Karpathy's autoresearch outer loop, Anthropic's skill-creator evaluation engine, and Stanford Meta-Harness's trace diagnosis concept. It enables AI Skills to autonomously iterate, evaluate, roll back, and optimize like training a model, validated by 19 rounds of zero-rollback self-evolution and a real business scenario.
metaData.summary: Starting from the pain points of stability, boundaries, and rule conflicts encountered in AI Skill development, the author systematically proposes a training framework for Skill self-evolution—skill-evolver. Drawing an analogy to the deep learning training paradigm, the framework treats Skill as a trainable object and designs an 8-stage iterative loop, a three-tier evaluation pipeline (L1 Quick Gatekeeper, L2 Dev Eval, L3 Strict Eval), a 5-dimensional AND gating mechanism, and a Trace diagnosis method based on original execution traces. The author validates the framework's effectiveness by having skill-evolver self-evolve for 19 rounds (all passing gating with zero rollbacks) and a real customer service Q&A Skill optimization case (recall rate improved from 86% to 98.67%). The article concludes by discussing practical challenges such as LLM evaluation noise, GT quality ceiling, and cost, while emphasizing the engineering principle of 'verify at every step' and the complementary value of AI in exploring beyond human cognitive boundaries.
metaData.featuredReason: This piece reframes Skill authoring as an engineering loop: trainable, evaluable, and rollbackable. Its eight-stage cycle, three-layer evaluation pipeline, five-dimensional AND gate, and trace-based diagnosis make self-evolving Skills concrete rather than speculative. It is worth reading for anyone building reliable agent workflows and evaluation systems.

mainPoints.point: A Skill should not be a handcrafted artifact, but an object that can be trained, rolled back, and optimized.
mainPoints.explanation: The author proposes drawing from the deep learning training paradigm, transforming Skill development from manual debugging to data-driven iterative optimization. The core is to define GT data and evaluation metrics, allowing the loop to automatically converge toward the goal.

mainPoints.point: The skill-evolver framework fuses three proven concepts: the outer loop skeleton, the evaluation engine, and trace diagnosis.
mainPoints.explanation: The framework integrates Karpathy's autoresearch iterative loop, Anthropic's skill-creator evaluation capabilities, and Stanford Meta-Harness's raw trace-driven diagnosis, forming a complete closed loop.

mainPoints.point: 5-dimensional AND gating and layered mutation are key engineering constraints ensuring iteration quality.
mainPoints.explanation: Through AND logic gating across 5 dimensions (e.g., quality, cost, safety), it eliminates the possibility of a high score in one dimension masking issues in others. Layered mutation controls the granularity of changes, gradually escalating from low-cost modifications to avoid blind large-scale changes.

mainPoints.point: The core value of meta-evolution lies in exploring boundaries that human developers cannot reach.
mainPoints.explanation: The 19 rounds of self-evolution uncovered 14 test cases the author had never thought of. These cases stemmed from real issues discovered by the tool during actual operation, not from manual presets, demonstrating AI's unique value in exploring cognitive blind spots.

keyQuotes: Writing a Skill that can run is not hard—you can throw together a SKILL.md and the model will follow it. But making it work reliably is a different story.
Instead of writing longer prompts to 'convince' it to follow rules, write the rules into code—if the gating function fails, just git revert HEAD, no negotiation.
The most valuable thing about meta-evolution is not the time saved by automation; it's that it runs a path for a user you've never met, a path you yourself would never traverse.
A Skill should not be a handcrafted artifact; it should be an object that can be trained, rolled back, and optimized.
Humans optionally contribute at the edge.

relatedArticles.title: GPT-5.4 Released: OpenAI's First Unified Model, Truly Native
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.4, creating the first unified Agent model that supports native Computer Use by integrating reasoning, coding, and computer interaction.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: From 7.9% to 54% Adoption: The Three-Stage Evolution of Kuaishou's Intelligent Code Review
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the three-generation architectural evolution of Kuaishou's intelligent code review system—from pure LLM heuristics to knowledge engine-driven, and finally to Agentic autonomous decision-making—increasing the CR adoption rate from 7.9% to 54%.

relatedArticles.title: RAG is Dead? No, Grep is Back!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the leaked source code of Claude Code, this article deeply deconstructs its abandonment of RAG and vector retrieval in favor of an LLM-driven multi-round iterative Grep search mechanism. It compares this approach with Cursor and Codex, demonstrating the feasibility and design philosophy of a zero-index solution in code search scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: 5 Lessons Learned from 400 Million Tokens: What Happened When 6 AI Agents Wrote Code for 4 Days Straight?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through a four-day multi-agent automated programming experiment, this article reveals that 'glue code' and engineering stability are more challenging and critical than prompt design when building AI systems.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Thinking About Agentic Engineering from First Principles
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically derives six core best practices for Agentic Engineering from first principles and introduces a modular, Skill-based open-source framework, aiming to combine engineering discipline with AI capabilities to reliably improve software engineering quality under complex constraints.

relatedArticles.title: The Evolution of Agent/Skills/Teams Architectures and Principles of Technology Selection
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically reviews the evolutionary trajectory of AI Agents from monolithic to multi-agent, then to Skills pluginization and Teams parallel collaboration, and, drawing on the latest research from Google and Anthropic, provides a scientific methodology for selection.
